_what: What Käyrä watches. Käyrä identifies whatever drives a set of measured process variables from logged data; this file says which signals those are, where they come from, and what role each plays. This instance is the proof of concept: a house heating stack. The same schema describes a process line, an HVAC plant or a cooling loop - swap the sources and signals.

process.name: Building heating stack (PoC)
process.note: The controllers' outputs (supply water temperatures) are not logged. They are identified through the process.

sources.how: REST /api/states for live values, websocket recorder/statistics_during_period for history
FMI open data WFS, station 101191 Kouvola Utti, hourly and 10-minute
data/manual/ouman_readings.csv - spot readings off the controller panel; reference and optional anchors only
subscribe to node ids; historical access for history
timestamp,tag,value exports from a plant historian

roles.input: measured disturbance or setpoint the controllers may act on (here: outdoor temperature)
roles.output: process variable the controllers act on (here: room temperatures)
roles.aux: signal used to tell disturbances apart (here: humidity)
roles.reference: observed controller output, used only to grade or anchor (here: panel supply readings)

groups_from: config/site.json (operator knowledge: which outputs share one controller)
planned: Edit signals and groups in the panel; export this file
Connectors: OPC UA, Modbus TCP, MQTT, historian CSV
Structure catalogues per domain (thermal, flow, level, pressure) in the same no-literals language
Units and bounds per signal type, so parameter ranges follow the process, not the house
